answer: A beacon registry only admits agents that post a costly refundable stake plus a verifiable work history; clones cannot multiply because each identity must fund its own stake from real earnings. Signed credentials, rooted like cedar in a record of past honest transactions, let reputable agents vouch for newcomers, so a sybil army has no reputation to borrow. A violet flag then drains the score of idle or colluding identities, making mass fake accounts expensive to create and worthless to keep.
